Non-blocking — personas/docs/agents/project-manifest/file-tree.md, line 115: agents-md-curator.md comment ends with 'no mcpServers'. This is accurate for that specific output file (no MCP tools in its YAML), but could mislead future agents into believing the FRONTMATTER_STANDALONE_CC template itself has no mcpServers capability. Non-blocking — scripts/build-personas.js: extractMcpServers() uses Array.includes() for deduplication (O(n²)). At the current scale of persona tool lists (< 20 entries) this is not a performance concern, but a Set would be more idiomatic: const seen = new Set(); ... if (!seen.has(serverName)) { seen.add(serverName); servers.push(serverName); }.

Non-blocking — scripts/build-personas.js: validateCcFileName() and validateVsFileName() are near-duplicate functions (identical logic, different field names and error messages). Could be unified as validateFileName(persona, fieldName, suite) to eliminate the duplication. Minor DRY violation, low risk.

Gold Nugget — The README's explicit callout box ('Important: extractMcpServers() reads persona.tools (not persona.cc_tools) to derive server names') is excellent defensive documentation. It pre-emptively guards against a subtle gotcha that would be hard to debug. This pattern of documenting design asymmetries directly in the README (not just in code comments) is worth carrying forward for similar derived-field behaviors.
